04 / A little more Sparsha

A non-linear route.
A very clear thread.

Computer science. A master's in cybersecurity at the University of York. A newsroom. An independent publication. And now, brand and creative strategy for a deeply technical business.

That route taught me to get comfortable with complexity—and to notice when the story is getting lost inside it.

Today, I lead a six-person team across content, design, and SEO. I work with engineering, sales, and leadership to connect product understanding, creative direction, and the commercial reason behind the brief.

Get close enough to ask better questions.

The useful question is often one layer below the brief. What are we really solving? Who needs to understand this? What would make them believe us?

Make the direction usable.

A team needs more than “make it creative.” A clear brief, a shared standard, and thoughtful feedback make good work repeatable without making it predictable.

Follow the idea through.

The work doesn't end at approval. I care about what happens after it goes live: who engages, what they do next, and what we should change.

A note from the margins / 01

The audience doesn't owe us their attention. The work has to earn it.
